newsitem.title: UK: Rolls has oil cure for Trent-700 engine fault.
newsitem.headline: Rolls has oil cure for Trent-700 engine fault.

text.p: Aero-engines firm Rolls-Royce Plc said on Tuesday it expects to solve a problem with its Trent 700 engines within the next three weeks, after tests showed the fault lay in the gearbox lubrication system. Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) grounded their 15 Trent-powered Airbus A330-300 aircraft on Saturday, following a series of mid-air engine shutdowns.
"We are looking at replacing the oil system," Rolls' chief spokesman Peter Barnes-Wallis told Reuters.

"There is insufficient oil lubricating the gearbox and the bearing becomes hot," he said. "We ran the fixed gearbox at the weekend and that did the trick -- it keeps the bearings at the right temperature."
Barnes-Wallis said engineers had found the solution to improving oilflow in the gearbox for the bigger Trent 800 turbofan, where the lubricating system was different.
It was now a matter of getting the solution approved by the aviation authorities, the airlines and Airbus ARBUS.CN.
"We think we can be within days of implementing this if everything goes according to plan, but certainly it cannot take longer than two to three weeks," he said.

Cathay, which operates 11 Trent-powered A330s and Dragon which operates four, stopped operating the aircraft after Dragonair suffered another engine failure on Friday on a flight from Hong Kong to Malaysia.
Rolls-Royce declines to comment on how much it might have to pay Cathay and Dragonair in compensation.
Meanwhile Indonesian carrier Garuda, which is the only other airline currently operating the Trent-powered A330, said on Tuesday that it would continue operating its six A330s.
Barnes-Wallis said all Trent-700 engines in service would be modified but it was believed that Garuda's engines were not at risk because they were so new.
"It's a problem that seems to deteriorate with age," he said. "They (the Garuda aircraft) entered service only late last year whereas Cathay have had some of these aircraft for a couple of years."

But Rolls also has orders outstanding for a further 48 Trent-powered A330s worth an estimated $960 million for the engines, based on a list price of $10 million apiece, plus options for a further 12 aircraft.
